newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: McCreevy named as new Irish finance minister.
newsitem.headline: McCreevy named as new Irish finance minister.

text.p: Irish prime minister Bertie Ahern on Thursday named Charlie McCreevy as finance minister in his new minority government to oversee the nation's entry into economic and monetary union (EMU).
McCreevy, a 47-year old accountant, has served as Minster for Social Welfare and Tourism and Trade in previous governments and replaces Labour's Ruairi Quinn in the post.
He has promised to cut tax rates by the autumn and has also set a tough target of four percent nominal growth for public expenditure each year.
McCreevy inherits a booming economy which has enjoyed a growth rate of 25 percent over the last three years while inflation remained below two percent.
He takes charge of the Irish economy in the crucial run-up to European economic and monetary union (EMU).
